questions.stem: World Environment Day is observed every year on:
questions.explanation: World Environment Day is observed on 5 June, established by the UN in 1972 (first held 1974). 22 April is Earth Day; 16 September is World Ozone Day; 1 December is World AIDS Day. World Environment Day 2023 was hosted by Côte d'Ivoire with the theme on plastic pollution.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: International Women's Day is celebrated on:
questions.explanation: International Women's Day is celebrated on 8 March globally. 11 February is the International Day of Women and Girls in Science; 24 January is National Girl Child Day (India); 19 November is International Men's Day. IWD highlights women's rights and gender equality.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: National Science Day in India is observed on 28 February to commemorate:
options: The discovery of the Raman Effect
questions.explanation: National Science Day is observed on 28 February to commemorate the discovery of the Raman Effect by Sir C.V. Raman on this day in 1928, for which he won the 1930 Nobel Prize in Physics. It promotes scientific temper. C.V. Raman's birthday is actually 7 November.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: World Health Day is observed on 7 April, marking the founding of which organisation?
questions.explanation: World Health Day is observed on 7 April, marking the founding of the World Health Organization (WHO) in 1948. Each year has a health theme. World Red Cross Day is 8 May; World Children's Day (UNICEF-associated) is 20 November.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Teachers' Day is celebrated in India on 5 September, the birthday of:
questions.explanation: Teachers' Day in India is celebrated on 5 September, the birthday of Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, the philosopher, scholar, and second President of India. Children's Day is 14 November (Nehru's birthday). World Teachers' Day (UNESCO) is observed globally on 5 October.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: International Yoga Day, proposed by India at the UN, is observed on:
questions.explanation: International Day of Yoga is observed on 21 June (the summer solstice, the longest day in the Northern Hemisphere). Proposed by PM Narendra Modi at the UN in 2014, it was first observed in 2015. 1 July is National Doctors' Day in India (birthday of Dr. B.C. Roy).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: World Earth Day is observed globally on:
questions.explanation: Earth Day is observed on 22 April, first held in 1970, to demonstrate support for environmental protection. 22 March is World Water Day; 5 June is World Environment Day; 11 July is World Population Day. Earth Day is now coordinated globally by EarthDay.org.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: National Youth Day in India is celebrated on 12 January, the birthday of:
questions.explanation: National Youth Day is celebrated on 12 January, the birth anniversary of Swami Vivekananda, to inspire the youth with his ideals. Subhas Chandra Bose's birthday (23 January) is now celebrated as Parakram Diwas. Bhagat Singh, Rajguru and Sukhdev's martyrdom (23 March) is Shaheed Diwas.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: World Water Day is observed on:
questions.explanation: World Water Day is observed on 22 March, established by the UN in 1993 to highlight the importance of freshwater. Each year has a theme (e.g., groundwater, water for peace). 22 April is Earth Day; 16 September is World Ozone Day.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Human Rights Day is observed worldwide on 10 December to commemorate:
options: The adoption of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (1948)
The end of World War II
questions.explanation: Human Rights Day is observed on 10 December, marking the adoption of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) by the UN General Assembly in 1948. UN Day (founding of the UN) is 24 October. India's National Human Rights Commission was established on 12 October 1993.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: World Ozone Day (International Day for the Preservation of the Ozone Layer) is observed on:
questions.explanation: World Ozone Day is observed on 16 September, commemorating the signing of the Montreal Protocol (1987) on substances that deplete the ozone layer. It is one of the most successful environmental treaties. 2 December is National Pollution Control Day (India), marking the Bhopal gas tragedy anniversary.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: National Constitution Day (Samvidhan Divas) is observed in India on:
questions.explanation: Constitution Day (Samvidhan Divas) is observed on 26 November, marking the day the Constituent Assembly adopted the Constitution of India in 1949 (it came into effect on 26 January 1950, Republic Day). It was first observed in 2015, the 125th birth anniversary year of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: World Population Day is observed on:
questions.explanation: World Population Day is observed on 11 July, established by the UN in 1989, inspired by the 'Day of Five Billion' (11 July 1987) when world population reached 5 billion. 1 May is International Labour Day; 21 March includes International Day of Forests and World Down Syndrome Day.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: National Unity Day (Rashtriya Ekta Diwas) is observed on 31 October, the birth anniversary of:
questions.explanation: National Unity Day is observed on 31 October, the birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, the 'Iron Man of India' who integrated 562 princely states into the Union. The Statue of Unity (Gujarat), the world's tallest statue, honours him. 31 October is also Indira Gandhi's death anniversary.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: International Day of Non-Violence is observed on 2 October, the birthday of:
questions.explanation: The International Day of Non-Violence is observed on 2 October, the birthday of Mahatma Gandhi (Gandhi Jayanti), declared by the UN in 2007. 2 October is also the birthday of Lal Bahadur Shastri, India's second PM. The day honours Gandhi's philosophy of ahimsa (non-violence).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: World Earth Hour, when people switch off lights for one hour, is organised by:
questions.explanation: Earth Hour is organised annually by the WWF (World Wide Fund for Nature), held on the last Saturday of March, when individuals and businesses switch off non-essential lights for one hour to raise climate-change awareness. It started in Sydney in 2007 and is now global.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: National Voters' Day in India is observed on 25 January to mark the founding of:
questions.explanation: National Voters' Day is observed on 25 January, marking the foundation day of the Election Commission of India (established 25 January 1950). First observed in 2011, it aims to encourage voter enrolment, especially among newly-eligible young voters. Republic Day is the very next day, 26 January.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: World Press Freedom Day is observed on:
questions.explanation: World Press Freedom Day is observed on 3 May, proclaimed by the UN in 1993, to celebrate press freedom and assess media freedom worldwide. 16 November is National Press Day in India (marking the Press Council of India's start of functioning). 8 September is International Literacy Day.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: International Literacy Day is observed on:
questions.explanation: International Literacy Day is observed on 8 September, declared by UNESCO in 1966 to highlight the importance of literacy. 5 October is World Teachers' Day; 24 October is United Nations Day; 10 December is Human Rights Day.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: National Farmers' Day (Kisan Diwas) in India is celebrated on 23 December, the birthday of:
questions.explanation: National Farmers' Day (Kisan Diwas) is celebrated on 23 December, the birth anniversary of Chaudhary Charan Singh, the fifth Prime Minister of India known for his pro-farmer policies. Lal Bahadur Shastri coined 'Jai Jawan Jai Kisan'; M.S. Swaminathan is the 'Father of the Green Revolution in India'.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: World Tuberculosis (TB) Day is observed on 24 March because on this day in 1882:
options: Robert Koch announced the discovery of the TB-causing bacterium
The first TB vaccine was administered
questions.explanation: World TB Day is observed on 24 March, marking the day in 1882 when Dr. Robert Koch announced his discovery of Mycobacterium tuberculosis, the bacterium causing TB. This paved the way for diagnosis and cure. The BCG vaccine (against TB) was developed later by Calmette and Guérin.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: National Statistics Day is observed in India on 29 June, the birth anniversary of:
questions.explanation: National Statistics Day is observed on 29 June, the birth anniversary of Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis, the 'Father of Indian Statistics', founder of the Indian Statistical Institute (ISI) and architect of the Second Five Year Plan. The Mahalanobis distance is named after him. C.R. Rao was his renowned student.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: World Biodiversity Day (International Day for Biological Diversity) is observed on:
questions.explanation: International Day for Biological Diversity is observed on 22 May, marking the adoption of the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) in 1992. 3 March is World Wildlife Day; 2 February is World Wetlands Day (Ramsar Convention); 11 December is International Mountain Day.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: National Technology Day is observed in India on 11 May to commemorate:
questions.explanation: National Technology Day is observed on 11 May, commemorating the successful Pokhran-II nuclear tests (Operation Shakti) conducted on 11 May 1998 under PM Atal Bihari Vajpayee and led by Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam. On the same day, India also test-fired the Trishul missile and a new aircraft (Hansa-3).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: World Wetlands Day is observed on 2 February to mark the adoption of which international treaty?
questions.explanation: World Wetlands Day is observed on 2 February, marking the adoption of the Ramsar Convention on Wetlands on 2 February 1971 in Ramsar, Iran. India has numerous Ramsar sites (over 75). The Montreal Protocol concerns ozone; the Kyoto Protocol and Paris Agreement concern climate change.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: National Sports Day in India is observed on 29 August every year. The date marks the birth anniversary of which sporting legend?

options.option_text: Milkha Singh, four-time Asian Games champion and sprint icon
Major Dhyan Chand, three-time Olympic gold medallist in hockey
P.T. Usha, sprint legend popularly known as the Payyoli Express
Kapil Dev, India's World Cup-winning captain in cricket in 1983

questions.explanation: 29 August is the birthday of Major Dhyan Chand (1905–1979), the hockey wizard who led India to Olympic gold in 1928, 1932, and 1936. The Government of India declared it National Sports Day in 2012. Milkha Singh is a common distractor but his birthday is 20 November; he has no National Day linked to him.

questions.stem: Samvidhan Divas (Constitution Day) is observed on 26 November in India. Which specific event in India's constitutional history does this date commemorate?

options.option_text: The Indian Independence Act receiving Royal Assent in the British Parliament
The Constituent Assembly formally adopting the Constitution of India
The Constitution of India coming into full legal force across the country
Dr. Ambedkar presenting the final draft Constitution to the Constituent Assembly

questions.explanation: On 26 November 1949 the Constituent Assembly adopted the Constitution of India. Option C is a common mistake — the Constitution came into force on 26 January 1950 (Republic Day), not on 26 November. The Government of India officially designated 26 November as Samvidhan Divas in 2015.

questions.stem: National Mathematics Day is observed in India on 22 December each year. This date honours the birth anniversary of which Indian mathematician, renowned for his path-breaking work in number theory and infinite series?

options.option_text: Brahmagupta, who formalised arithmetic rules for operations involving zero
Aryabhata, who approximated the value of pi and explained Earth's axial rotation
Srinivasa Ramanujan, self-taught genius born on 22 December 1887 in Erode
P.C. Mahalanobis, statistician who founded the Indian Statistical Institute

questions.explanation: Srinivasa Ramanujan was born on 22 December 1887. The Government of India declared his birthday National Mathematics Day in 2012. Brahmagupta (7th century) and Aryabhata (5th century) are plausible distractors as celebrated Indian mathematicians, but neither has a birth anniversary on 22 December. P.C. Mahalanobis is linked to Statistics Day (29 June).

questions.stem: National Voters' Day is observed in India on 25 January each year. The date marks the founding anniversary of which constitutional body?

options.option_text: The Supreme Court of India, set up under the Constitution in January 1950
The Election Commission of India, established on 25 January 1950
The Union Public Service Commission, India's central recruitment authority
The Comptroller and Auditor General's office, constituted under Article 148

questions.explanation: The Election Commission of India was established on 25 January 1950, one day before the Constitution came into force. The Government of India observes this as National Voters' Day since 2011 to encourage voter registration. The Supreme Court was also set up in 1950 but on 28 January — a common distractor confusion.

questions.stem: World Press Freedom Day is observed on 3 May each year. On the recommendation of which body did the United Nations General Assembly formally proclaim this observance?

options.option_text: The UN Human Rights Council, following the 1993 Vienna Human Rights Declaration
Reporters Without Borders, an international press-freedom advocacy watchdog
UNESCO, following its 1991 General Conference declaration issued in Belgrade, Serbia
The International Federation of Journalists at its annual world congress in 1992

questions.explanation: UNESCO's General Conference in 1991 in Windhoek, Namibia (not Belgrade) issued the Windhoek Declaration on press freedom, leading UNESCO to recommend 3 May as World Press Freedom Day. The UN General Assembly then proclaimed it in 1993. Option A (UN Human Rights Council) is a frequent wrong answer because of the Vienna Declaration's proximity in time.

questions.stem: The International Day for the Preservation of the Ozone Layer is observed on 16 September each year. This date specifically marks the signing of which landmark international environmental agreement?

options.option_text: The Vienna Convention for the Protection of the Ozone Layer, signed in 1985
The Montreal Protocol on Substances that Deplete the Ozone Layer, 1987
The Kyoto Protocol, the first legally binding framework to cut greenhouse emissions
The Kigali Amendment to the Montreal Protocol, adopted in Rwanda in 2016

questions.explanation: The Montreal Protocol was signed on 16 September 1987 — hence the UN General Assembly designated 16 September as the ozone preservation day (Resolution 49/114, 1994). Option A is a very common wrong answer: the Vienna Convention (1985) is the parent treaty, but it was signed on 22 March, not 16 September. The Kigali Amendment (2016) deals with HFCs under the same protocol but is not what the date commemorates.

questions.stem: 'Pravasi Bharatiya Diwas' (Non-Resident Indians Day) is observed in India on 9 January every year. Which historical event linked to the Indian diaspora does this date specifically commemorate?

options.option_text: Mahatma Gandhi's departure from India to South Africa as a young barrister in 1893
Mahatma Gandhi's return to India from South Africa on 9 January 1915
The enactment of the Overseas Citizenship of India scheme under the 2003 amendment
The first Pravasi Bharatiya Sammelan convention held in New Delhi in the year 2003

questions.explanation: 9 January 1915 was the date Mahatma Gandhi returned to India from South Africa after 21 years, marking the arrival of one of history's most celebrated members of the Indian diaspora. Pravasi Bharatiya Diwas was instituted in 2003 (first held 9 January 2003), but the date itself commemorates Gandhi's 1915 homecoming. Option A (departure in 1893) is the classic reversal trap — Gandhi left India on May 1893, not 9 January.
